text:
Eric: Heads up — we need to settle rerank scoring units and routing before the console change this week. Question: do we bill/quotas per-candidate score or per-request? cc @Maya @Jess

Maya: my vote: per-candidate. Reason: cost scales with model compute per candidate. Otherwise customers can send 1000 candidates and pay same as 1.

Jess: +1 per-candidate for fairness, but we need a soft cap to avoid DoS via huge candidate lists. Maybe a per-request hard limit + per-candidate billing.

Tom: related: scoring format. Do we return normalized score [0-1], logit, or both? analytics pipeline expects stable numbers.

Maya: prefer normalized + meta raw_score if teams want it. Normalized helps UI and AB tests. Example payload:

```json
{
  "candidates": [{"id":"c1","score":0.82,"raw_score":3.4}, {"id":"c2","score":0.31,"raw_score":1.2}],
  "model":"redwood-rerank-v2"
}
```

Eric: How do we handle model selection and fallback? Customer pins model in config but we might want to fallback to cheaper variant on capacity.

Jess: suggest routing policy tiers: pinned -> preferred -> compatible. If pinned unavailable, respect customer opt-in fallback policy (canary/off). Add explicit header `x-rerank-fallback: allow|deny|cost-preferred`.

Tom: console UX must show when fallback happened and what model was used per request. Also expose per-candidate token counts and model-affinity telemetry.

Maya: telemetry: we need per-route histograms for latency per candidate, and a 95th percentile cost-per-request metric. Also add a "score-stability" regression alert that looks at delta in normalized scores on a held prompt set.

Eric: quotas: implement a two-axis quota: monthly candidate-units + per-minute request cap. Candidate-units = sum(num_candidates * weight_by_model). Weight_by_model accounts for model flops.

Jess: Good. Need an escape hatch for enterprise deployments: dedicated customers can opt into request-based billing for predictability.

Tom: Implementation concern: computing normalized score requires min/max calibration per model. That can drift. We might include `score_version` in response and dashboard.

Maya: Also add `score_format` enum: `normalized`, `raw`, `both`. Default `normalized`.

deploy-bot: deployment started for feature/rr-scoring-quota -> staging :gear:  (CI: 85% passed)

Eric: action items: Maya to write telemetry spec, Jess to draft quota + billing change, Tom to update API contract (include score_version/score_format), I'll add console flags for fallback visibility. Sync tomorrow 11am.

Maya: noted, will post spec PR.

Jess: I'll loop in billing and legal for rate changes.

Tom: will add sample event to /events schema.

Eric: thanks everyone :rocket:
